title: cuscuta epithymum subsp. planiflora
intro:
Cuscuta epithymum subsp. planiflora, commonly known as Dodder, is a parasitic plant that grows by attaching itself to the stems of other plants using its specialized leaves, thereby obtaining its nutrients.

This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory effects. The therapeutic actions of Cuscuta epithymum subsp. planiflora include its ability to promote wound healing, reduce fever, and alleviate respiratory issues such as bronchitis and asthma. The bioactive constituents of this plant include alkaloids, glycosides, and flavonoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
